mainEntity.name: How much does a Ford Kuga ST-Line 1.5 EcoBoost engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt or reconditioned Ford Kuga ST-Line 1.5 EcoBoost engine typically costs between £2,500 and £4,000, including supply and fit. Rebuilt units include upgraded components and a 12-month warranty. Main dealers often charge £5,000+ for the same replacement. Used engines are a popular budget alternative, starting from around £600.

mainEntity.name: Does the Ford Kuga 1.5 EcoBoost have the wet belt problem?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, the Ford Kuga 1.5 EcoBoost (including ST-Line variants) uses a "wet belt" (belt-in-oil) design. The timing belt runs inside the engine oil and can degrade over time. If not replaced preventatively (typically every 6 years or 60,000 miles), it sheds debris that blocks the oil pickup, causing catastrophic engine seizure. This is the single most common reason for Ford Kuga ST-Line 1.5 EcoBoost engine replacements.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Ford Kuga ST-Line 1.5 EcoBoost?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the vehicle's current market value and overall condition. For older Mk2 models valued under £9,000, a full rebuilt engine replacement may approach 40-50% of the vehicle's value, making a low-mileage used engine or preventative repair more sensible. For newer Mk3 models valued over £12,000, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine with a 12-month warranty is a financially sound investment to preserve the vehicle's sporty utility.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Ford Kuga ST-Line 1.5 EcoBoost engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A standard Ford Kuga ST-Line 1.5 EcoBoost engine swap typically takes 5 to 7 working days. This includes sourcing the correct engine code (e.g., M1JA, M1JC, or YYJA), nationwide delivery to your chosen specialist, and physical installation, fluid top-up, and comprehensive road testing.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the M1JA and YYJA Ford Kuga 1.5 EcoBoost engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both are 1.5-litre turbocharged petrol engines from the same EcoBoost family, but they belong to different generations. The M1JA (2015-2018) is a Mk2 engine producing 150 PS. The YYJA (2020-present) is a Mk3 engine available in 120 PS or 150 PS outputs, featuring updated engine management and start-stop technology. Both share the wet belt architecture, meaning the same preventative maintenance rules apply to both.

historyTimeline.h2: Ford Kuga ST-Line 1.5 EcoBoost - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the ST-Line trim was paired with the 1.5 EcoBoost engine, it brought sporty aesthetics and punchy performance to the Kuga range, though its "wet belt" architecture requires vigilant maintenance to prevent catastrophic failure.

milestones.description: M1JA (150 PS) introduced in the Ford Kuga Mk2 ST-Line, establishing the 1.5-litre turbocharged petrol as the performance-oriented choice for the trim.
M1JC / M1JJ (150 PS) introduced with minor revisions to the wet belt and oil pump drive belt materials following early wear concerns, though the core belt-in-oil architecture remained.

YYJA / YYJB (120 PS / 150 PS) introduced in the Ford Kuga Mk3 ST-Line, featuring improved overall durability and start-stop technology, but still requiring strict adherence to Ford-specific oil change intervals.

problems.h4: Wet Belt Degradation & Oil Starvation - Why the Ford Kuga ST-Line 1.5 EcoBoost Wears Prematurely
problems.affectedModels: Ford Kuga ST-Line 1.5 EcoBoost (M1JA, M1JC, M1JJ, YYJA, 2015-present)
problems.rootCause: The timing belt runs in engine oil. Over time, petrol contamination and heat cause the belt to degrade, shedding rubber debris that blocks the oil pump pickup strainer, leading to a drop in oil pressure and catastrophic engine seizure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacing the wet belt, oil pump drive belt, and full oil system flush before failure occurs.
repairOptions.longevity: Highly recommended at 60k miles or 6 years to avoid engine replacement.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The only viable option once oil starvation has caused bearing damage or seizure.

problems.recommendation: If your Ford Kuga ST-Line 1.5 EcoBoost is showing early warning signs (rattling on cold start, coolant loss, or oil pressure warning), pursue preventative belt replacement or cooling system repair immediately. If the engine has already seized or suffered severe overheating, a reconditioned or rebuilt unit is the most reliable long-term solution, provided the vehicle's value justifies the investment.

problems.h4: Coolant Intrusion & Head Gasket Failure - Secondary Ford Kuga ST-Line 1.5 EcoBoost Vulnerabilities
problems.affectedModels: Ford Kuga ST-Line 1.5 EcoBoost (M1JA, M1JC, early YYJA)
problems.rootCause: Early iterations of the 1.5 EcoBoost block exhibited porosity or head gasket weaknesses, allowing coolant to seep into the combustion chambers, leading to overheating and potential hydrolock if ignored.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Stripping the top end, machining the head, and replacing the gasket and seals.
repairOptions.longevity: Viable only if the block is not warped or cracked from overheating.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Required if overheating has warped the cylinder head or cracked the block.
